name: Advanced reactors (high-temperature gas, molten salt)
principle: Generation IV concepts cool with helium, molten salt, sodium or lead for higher outlet temperatures and process heat. The WNA page says HTGRs use helium at up to 950 °C and TRISO fuel stable to 1,600 °C, and describes China's HTR-PM at Shidaowan (210 MWe from two 105 MWe modules, 750 °C outlet, about 40% efficiency) as a demonstration plant under construction when the page was written.

advantages: High outlet temperature suits refining and hydrogen heat
limitations: The WNA page is dated: it does not cover Xe-100, Hermes or Natrium

reference_plants.name: HTR-PM demonstration plant, Shidaowan, China (CNNC/Huaneng/Tsinghua)
reference_plants.capacity: world's first high-temperature gas-cooled reactor pebble-bed module plant; two 105 MWe reactor modules; grid-connected December 2021, commercial operation from December 2023; 750 C core-outlet helium, 566 C steam

source.note: CNNC: "the world's first High Temperature gas cooled Reactor of Pebble bed Module (HTR-PM) is now connected to the grid"; core-outlet 750 C / steam 566 C from world-energy.org, 24 Aug 2021 (fuel loading); commercial operation Dec 2023 widely reported; read 2026-10-28
